_readme: THE STRATEGY PLANNER'S FRAMEWORKS, AS DATA. To-do item 15.1, Decision 3 of
design/mockups/strategy-planner.html, ruled by Mike 2026-09-16: a framework is DATA
naming its capture shape, and is NEVER its own screen. Five shapes cover all 45
frameworks the four Planning Domains hold, and a mentor adds the 46th by typing.
🔴 A NEW .vue FILE NAMED AFTER A FRAMEWORK IS THE THING THAT RULING REFUSED. If a
framework will not fit a shape, the answer is a new SHAPE - one more for all 45 - never
a component for that one framework.
🔴 THE CONCEPT TEXT IS NOT HERE, AND MUST NOT BE COPIED HERE. Each framework points at
a material in a domain support file via `material`, and the loader joins them. Those
summaries are authored, reach the AI, and are edited in one place; a second copy here
would drift from the first and nothing would fail. The three domain support files are
strategy-, sales-marketing- and staff-domain-support.json - two of the four Planning
Domains live outside the strategy file, which is why the loader reads across all three.
WHAT IS HERE THAT IS NOWHERE ELSE: `helpsClientTo`, from Mike's own Session Scope
tables in ADV.0 Planning Outcomes; the capture SHAPE; and the per-field PROMPTS, which
are the deck's own words and are what make a framework a facilitated conversation
rather than an empty grid.
THREE FRAMEWORKS, NOT FORTY-FIVE, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. Mike's ruling: 'Build the
machine and prove it on three frameworks, not fifty.' These three were chosen because
they need three genuinely DIFFERENT shapes - if one renderer carries all three, the
remaining 42 are data entry. The other 42 are added here, not in code.
SHAPES: 'buckets' (sort ideas under named headings), 'quadrants' (exactly four boxes),
'forces' (five or six boxes, one marked centre). Two more are expected and are NOT yet
built: 'placement' (a 2x2 an owner is placed on - the Heald Matrix, Business Dating)
and 'actions' (a Task / Whom / When table). Adding one is a change to the renderer and
to STRATEGY_SHAPES in server/utils/strategyFrameworks.js, and to nothing else.

frameworks.name: The 8 Profit Levers
frameworks.helpsClientTo: Identify the little things that can contribute to massive business growth.
frameworks.captureInstruction: If you're running short of time you can identify just one task per lever for now; do the rest when time provides.

model.note: Decision 5, RULED AGAINST THE RECOMMENDATION: this runs INSIDE the framework card on the same backend route as the standalone page. Seamless is the surface, never a second copy of the maths.

fields.label: Number of Foot-traffic
fields.prompt: Gain their ATTENTION — market attention, outbound message views.

fields.label: Number of Prospects
fields.prompt: Capture their INTEREST — shop walk-ins, phone-ins or social click-thru.

fields.label: Number of Customers
fields.prompt: Secure their CUSTOM — the percentage of prospects that become customers.

fields.label: Average Customer Spend
fields.prompt: Secure their CUSTOM — total sales value divided by total number of transactions.

fields.label: Average Customer Frequency
fields.prompt: Keep them WANTING MORE — how often do they buy per month or year.

fields.label: Sales Margin
fields.prompt: Buy materials or stock FOR LESS — the difference between how much you sell it for and what it cost you.

fields.label: Activity Driven Costs
fields.prompt: Reduce SPENDING — the cost of gaining a customer.

fields.label: Fixed Costs (Overheads)
fields.prompt: Reduce SPENDING/OVERHEADS — the total regular cost of being open for business, even when nobody buys.

frameworks.name: SWOT / PEST
frameworks.helpsClientTo: Establish a baseline of where they actually stand before anything is planned.
frameworks.captureInstruction: You don't have to complete them in any set order — just record them as they come to mind.

fields.label: Strengths
fields.prompt: Internal — personnel roles, communication lines, POS report accuracy, profit lines, technology usage.

fields.label: Weaknesses
fields.prompt: Internal — growth drag, and the financial instruments used to reduce risk.

fields.label: Opportunities
fields.prompt: External (PEST) — political, economic, interest rate, consumer confidence, regulatory or tariff changes.

fields.label: Threats
fields.prompt: External (PEST) — the same prompts, read the other way.

frameworks.name: Porter's 5 Forces
frameworks.helpsClientTo: Look out for changes in the market and anticipate how everyone will react, so they can be ready to take advantage of the situation.
frameworks.captureInstruction: You don't have to follow any particular order; just capture your thoughts as you go.

fields.label: Customers
fields.prompt: Are customers likely to be motivated to pay premium prices in return for latest style or fashion, technology or prestige? Are they concerned about your business safety, environment or ethical impact?

fields.label: New Entrants
fields.prompt: How easy is it for new entrants to enter your marketplace? Is it conceivable that your current supplier could become your future competition?

fields.label: Suppliers
fields.prompt: Is there competition amongst your suppliers? Do they actively compete for your business, and if you had to shift to a new supplier, how easy would it be?

fields.label: Substitutes
fields.prompt: What are the alternatives to your product or service? Could your customers solve their problem a different way?

fields.label: Existing Rivalry
fields.prompt: The centre of the model — what the other four press upon.

fields.label: Observations & response
fields.prompt: Record your observations AND your response to the changing economic environment — the deck asks for both, and a response is the half most easily lost.
